newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi tobacco deal seen topping $3 billion.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi tobacco deal seen topping $3 billion.

text.p: The settlement between cigrette makers and the state of Mississippi is expected to top $3 billion, a tobacco industry representative said Thursday.
"If you do the arithmetic, I believe the figure does go above $3 billion by the 25th year," industry spokesman Lance Morgan told Reuters.

Morgan was speaking after tobacco companies said an agreement in principle had been reached with Mississippi, which in 1994 became the first of 40 states to sue the tobacco industry for state tax money spent treating Medicaid recipients for smoking-related illnesses.
The $3 billion figure compares with about $940 million in damages sought by the state.

The tobacco companies said the accord would provide for a payment to Mississippi of $170 million by July 15. Beginning in December 1998, the state would receive a 1.7 percent share of the annual payments that are to be made to the states under last month's $368.5 billion national tobacco accord.
The Mississippi settlement enabled the industry to avoid a trial of the state's suit against it. The suit was to be the first to reach trial, with proceedings set to begin next Wednesday.
